activity.notes: Asparukh founded the medieval Bulgarian state after the Danubian Bulgar victory over Constantine IV in 680. Modern references differ slightly on the ruler's bounds: Encyclopaedia Iranica gives 679–701, while the conventional state foundation is associated with 681. ATLAS therefore uses c.681–c.701 for his rule of the First Bulgarian Empire and marks both boundaries approximate rather than manufacturing false precision.

sources.title: ASPARUKH — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Iranica identifies Asparukh as founder of the medieval Bulgarian state, gives his rule at Pliska as 679–701, and notes his decisive victory over Constantine IV in 680.

sources.title: KHAZARS — Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.citation_text: Iranica describes the Bulgar group led by Asparukh as moving west and establishing a conquest state in Byzantine Moesia around 679.
